source.quote: Prism Sound's own specification page for the Titan, read 2026-11-25. Digital Inputs section: « Formats supported - S/PDIF (RCA or TOSLINK), ADAT, ADAT S/MUX (TOSLINK) »; « Sample rates supported - S/PDIF (2 channel): 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4 and 192kHz / ADAT (8 channel) 44.1 and 48kHz / ADAT S/MUX (4 channel): 88.2 and 96kHz »; « Channel Status - ignored »; « Word-length - 24 bit »; « AES3 operation - via S/PDIF RCA, using RCA-XLR adaptor »; « Sample-rate converter (SRC) - Selectable at S/PDIF input; allowing input at any sample rate »; « Bit transparency - Maintained (allows recording of Dolby or DTS streams) ». Synchronization: « System sample rates - 44.1 / 48 / 88.2 / 96 / 176.4 / 192kHz »; « Sync sources: Master - local, Wordclock, DI (S/PDIF input) or ADAT ». Rear Panel: « Digital inputs - 1 x RCA / 1 x TOSLINK for S/PDIF or ADAT Optical input; (RCA can operate as AES3 input using XLR-RCA adapter) »; « Wordclock - 2 x BNC sockets, output and input (75R) »; « USB port - 1 x USB 2 port ». DSD, DoP and SACD appear nowhere on the page. No converter chip part number is named, no digital filter name or count is given, and no oversampling bypass is offered - a grep across every captured Prism Sound page for AK4, ES90, CS43, PCM17, WM87, Sabre, Burr-Brown, Asahi Kasei and Cirrus Logic returned zero matches.

facts.chip: No part number is published anywhere on Prism Sound's site, for any product.

_conditions_de_Prism_Sound_aucune_clause: Measured 2026-11-25. prismsound.io has NO terms-of-use page: /terms/, /terms-of-use/, /terms-and-conditions/, /legal/, /copyright/ and /disclaimer/ all 404, and the full 74-page sitemap lists only a privacy policy and one PDF. That PDF, « Audio Squadron Limited Terms & Conditions of Sale », is a 7-page image-only scan that was READ page by page: all 19 clauses, none forbidding the copying or reuse of content. Its nearest clauses do not reach website material - clause 14 disclaims warranties as to third-party IPR « in respect of the goods », clause 7's confidentiality binds Seller and Purchaser only and « expressly excludes public-domain information ». The only assertion of rights is the footer « (c) 2026 Audio Squadron Ltd. All rights reserved. » robots.txt on both hosts permits every product and spec path. So the sale terms were genuinely read and permit this; the website-use question has no document to answer it.
_le_fabricant_decline_lexactitude_de_ses: Clause 6(b) of the sale terms, worth recording because no other maker in this catalogue states it: « The Seller shall use reasonable endeavours to ensure the accuracy of technical data or literature relating to the goods, but the Seller accepts no liability [...] for any error or omission in such technical data or literature. » And every spec page carries « In keeping with our policy of continual development, specifications are subject to amendment without notice. E&OE. » The figures are still the maker's published figures and still the best source there is - but this is the only brand that says in a contract that they may be wrong.
_les_debits_ADAT_sechangent_contre_des_c: « ADAT (8 channel) 44.1 and 48kHz / ADAT S/MUX (4 channel): 88.2 and 96kHz ». On this interface the rate and the channel count cannot both be read from one figure: eight channels at 48 kHz, four at 96, and Prism offers no 176.4 or 192 kHz ADAT mode at all - its lists stop at S/MUX x2. inputs.adat records 96000, the highest rate the socket reaches, and the channel count it costs survives in this gloss. database/interfaces/adat.json holds the general rule.
_pourquoi_dsd_max_vaut_none_et_non_absen: DSD, DoP and SACD appear NOWHERE on this product's pages - and these are full engineering specifications, itemised socket by socket, with word lengths and channel-status rows. A professional interface with ADAT and word clock does not do DSD, and the complete absence of the word across a specification of this density is the maker's answer. Same reading as the Audient records, and deliberately NOT the reading given to Musical Fidelity's V90-DAC, where silence on a consumer page from a maker that advertises DSD elsewhere was left as absent.
_AUCUN_plafond_nest_publie_pour_la_conne: This is the central gap in Prism Sound's documentation and it is stated as an absence. The USB port appears ONLY as a connector count under Rear Panel - « USB port | 1 x USB 2 port » - with no audio format row anywhere on the page. The device figure recorded here comes from « System sample rates | 44.1 / 48 / 88.2 / 96 / 176.4 / 192kHz » in the Synchronization section, which is NOT labelled a USB ceiling and is not recorded as one: inputs.usb carries no figure. Titan, Atlas, Lyra 1, Lyra 2 and Orpheus are all like this. Callia is the only Prism product that states a USB audio-format row, and it is the only one whose USB ceiling turns out to exceed its S/PDIF ceiling.
_la_prise_optique_porte_DEUX_formats_et_: « 1 x RCA / 1 x TOSLINK for S/PDIF or ADAT Optical input ». One optical socket that is either S/PDIF or ADAT depending on how it is configured - not two inputs. The catalogue records both interfaces because both are reachable, and this gloss is the only place saying they are the same hole in the back panel and cannot be used at once.
_lhorloge_mot_nest_pas_une_entree_audio: « Wordclock - 2 x BNC sockets, output and input (75R) ». A timing reference, carrying no audio. Not recorded as an input. Nor is the RCA's AES3 capability a separate socket: « RCA can operate as AES3 input using XLR-RCA adapter » is the same coaxial input in another electrical mode, so no aes_ebu entry is written - a real AES/EBU XLR socket is a different thing and this device has none.
